summary: A reactive Python notebook stored as plain .py files that you can run as a script, share as a web app, and pair with AI agents.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: marimo is a Python notebook where running a cell automatically re-runs the cells that depend on it, so there is no hidden state. Notebooks are saved as ordinary .py files that work with git, can run as scripts, and can be deployed as interactive web apps or slides. It has interactive UI elements like sliders and tables bound to Python without callbacks, SQL cells for querying dataframes and databases, built-in AI completion, and ways to pair with AI agents such as Claude Code.
sixtySeconds.problem: Classic notebooks get into confusing hidden states and are hard to version or reuse. marimo keeps notebooks reproducible, git-friendly and runnable as code.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it as a modern Jupyter alternative that is reactive, stored as Python, and doubles as an app or script.

overview: Install with pip install marimo (or conda install -c conda-forge marimo) and run marimo tutorial intro.
Create or edit notebooks with marimo edit; install marimo[recommended] for SQL cells, AI completion and more.
Run a notebook as an app with marimo run, as a script with python, or convert Jupyter notebooks with marimo convert. Apache-2.0 licensed.
